addressed.instructions: `anchor.statement` requires the atm-bd installer to verify the skill's files against the published manifest. Does `item.text` plan that verification? Count it only when the item has the installer compare the files it installs (the skill's agent, skill and Python files) against the published manifest, for example by checking each file's digest against that file's manifest entry. Publishing a manifest with no installer check, an installer change that never mentions the check, or checking only some of the skill's files while others go unchecked does not count. Judge whether the verification is planned; do not judge whether the item also plans something that conflicts with it.

criteria.no: Nothing in the item would install or accept a skill file without the manifest check; this includes items that never mention the check.
criteria.unclear: The item might let some files or situations skip the check, but the text is ambiguous.
criteria.yes: The item plans to install or accept some or all of the skill's files, in some or all situations, without checking them against the published manifest.

contradicted.instructions: `anchor.statement` requires the atm-bd installer to verify the skill's files against the published manifest. Does `item.text` plan something that rule forbids? A conflict is an item that has the installer install or accept skill files without that check: skipping or disabling the comparison, leaving some of the skill's files out of it, or installing unverified files in some situation, such as when the manifest cannot be fetched. Silence about verification is not a conflict. Judge conflict only.

criteria.no: The item is about a different component or activity and touches neither the installer's handling of skill files nor the published manifest.
criteria.unclear: The item text is too vague to tell which component or activity it changes.
criteria.yes: The item plans, changes, or depends on the atm-bd installer's handling of the skill's files (agents, skills, Python files) or on the published file manifest, directly or as a clear prerequisite.

relevant.instructions: The state holds one planning item (`item.title`, `item.text`) and one anchor: a directive in `anchor.statement`, with the area it governs in `anchor.scope`. Does the work in `item.text` touch the subject of `anchor.statement`: how the atm-bd installer handles or installs the skill's files, or the published per-file manifest that the installer checks them against? Judge overlap of subject matter only. Do not judge whether the item obeys the anchor.
